Class RegulatedDifferentialDrive

java.lang.Object
io.github.jabrena.juno.robotics.navigation.RegulatedDifferentialDrive
public final class RegulatedDifferentialDrive extends Object
Drives a two-wheel robot by distance and heading, with its wheels regulated by a RegulatedPair (such as an RCX pair). Millimetre travel and in-place turns are converted to per-side encoder targets using DriveGeometry and submitted as one coordinated movement, so the two wheels start together.

Conversion uses only the geometry's calibrated values: each side's encoder degrees per wheel revolution, the wheel diameter and the effective track width. Positive travel is forward and a positive turn is counter-clockwise, so the left wheel turns backwards and the right forwards in a positive turn. Straight travel uses the same millimetres for both wheels, but each side's encoder ratio decides its target, so a robot whose sides are calibrated differently still covers the same distance on each wheel. Create it once at startup.

Left and right are the robot's, seen from behind as it drives forward, and the geometry's encoder ratios are the physical left and right wheels'. A build whose pair has its left side on the robot's right wheel is created with sidesSwapped, so a counter-clockwise turn still turns counter-clockwise.

    • pivotDegrees

      public void pivotDegrees(int degrees)
      Turns about one wheel by degrees (positive is counter-clockwise), and waits until it completes.

    • pivotDegrees

      public void pivotDegrees(int degrees, boolean immediateReturn)
      Turns about one wheel by degrees, positive counter-clockwise, returning at once when immediateReturn is set: the outer wheel, the right one for a counter-clockwise pivot, moves forward along an arc of the whole track width while the other stays. A pivot moves one wheel only, so its finest turn is one sensor step of one wheel, half an in-place turn's: a small heading correction.
      Throws:
      IllegalArgumentException - if the pivot is outside the supported range or quantizes to zero degrees

    • distanceMillimetres

      public int distanceMillimetres()
      How far the robot's centre is from the pair's zero, in millimetres: the average of the two wheels, each by its own encoder ratio, as the pair's last read found them. The difference of two readings is the travel in between.
